clue.text: Build another storey and create a great din

definitions.meaning: literally lifting the top of a house higher to add a floor
idiom for making a tremendous noise, as a cheering crowd does

explanation.surface: A builder adding a floor to a house makes a terrible racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for cheering loudly also reads literally as hoisting the top of a building, which is what adding a floor needs.

clue.text: Get-together for our nine constituents

indicators.note: constituents are the parts something is made up of, so the letters of the two words are rearranged to form a new whole

explanation.surface: A gathering of nine people, perhaps old classmates, described as making up a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people who have been apart is a synonym for a get-together.

clue.text: Ruler who was terribly vain

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the four letters of the following word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tsar whose terrible reputation was matched by his vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' nods to Ivan the Terrible, the sixteenth-century Russian tsar, while signalling the anagram of VAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar, so the name is an example of a ruler.

clue.text: Raise tax in eastern area of calm

indicators.note: in places the tax inside the area of calm

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side away from the wind, a calm area
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone proposes putting up taxes in a peaceful eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax; 'in' puts it inside LEE, the sheltered side out of the wind, after E for eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up is to raise it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Monotonous drone by the tom-tom

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
a tom-tom is a kind of drum

explanation.surface: A dull, repetitive sound made by someone beating a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and repetitive is humdrum, a synonym for monotonous.

clue.text: Manages to score in the cricket match

definitions.meaning: to run a business is to manage it
in cricket the score is counted in ...

explanation.surface: A player succeeds in scoring during a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the British bat-and-ball game, batsmen score by making runs between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in charge of something is to run it; and runs are the units of a cricket score.

clue.text: Open-air exit

definitions.meaning: taking place outside, not under a roof
read as two words, a door leading out

explanation.surface: A two-word description of an exit, read as an adjective for the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside activities happen in the open air, and a way out is literally a door to the outside.

clue.text: General practice of lawyers is to make real money

definitions.meaning: read as two words: what is current, or commonly done, in the legal profession
notes and coins a creditor must accept as genuine payment

explanation.surface: A remark that lawyers routinely make proper money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that must by law be accepted is legal tender; read literally, the phrase means what is current among lawyers.

clue.text: Much forbearance needed to produce a first-class Gilbert and Sullivan

parts.note: first-class means great, excellent
Patience is one of the comic operas by Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Putting on a top-quality production of a comic opera takes a lot of tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote the Victorian comic operas; one of them is Patience (1881).
explanation.definitionFit: A great deal of tolerance and endurance is a synonym of much forbearance.

clue.text: Gold coin found in Early English school

indicators.note: found in means placed within the other letters

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English, the medieval architectural style
a ducat is an old European gold coin

explanation.surface: A gold coin turned up at an old English school.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Keep an eye on the computer screen

definitions.meaning: to watch over or observe something
a computer's display unit

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch their computer display.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something closely is to monitor it, and a computer's display is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Surrounded by a shadowy reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: shadowy means dim, poorly lit

explanation.surface: Someone stands among faint reflections in the gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the middle of things is being among them, the sense of surrounded by.

clue.text: Hassle Henry

definitions.meaning: to harass or pester someone
the familiar form of the name Henry

explanation.surface: A command to pester a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is the traditional pet form of Henry, as with Prince Harry and Shakespeare's 'Harry' for Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harry them; and the name is the usual familiar form of Henry.

clue.text: Soft-drink business going to a Californian city

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A soft-drinks firm is relocating to California.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy brown beverage is a type of soft drink, an example of the category.

clue.text: The management team is utterly blase

indicators.note: read as 'when uttered', the word for being blase is spoken out loud and heard as another

parts.note: someone blase is bored and unimpressed

explanation.surface: Complaining that the directors are completely indifferent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'as uttered': BORED, the sense of blase, said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors sitting together form its board, the group in charge.

clue.text: The disadvantages of being caught in tights

definitions.meaning: drawbacks or hidden problems
a tear or pulled thread made when tights catch on something

explanation.surface: Complaining about the downside of getting hosiery caught on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawbacks are snags, and a snag is also a pull in fabric caused by catching on a sharp point.

clue.text: Turn a blind eye when the swindler gets swindled

parts.note: a con man, shortened to con, is a swindler
done means cheated, as in 'I've been done'

explanation.surface: A trickster gets tricked in turn, and everyone looks away.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook or pardon wrongdoing is to condone it, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Softaccompaniment to Hindu psalm can hold one captive

indicators.note: an accompaniment comes along with something, so this letter follows the chant

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred chant in Hinduism
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A quiet musical backing to a Hindu chant is so beautiful it captivates.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, the musical direction for soft) is the accompaniment, so it goes after MANTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set to catch people, such as a poacher, is something that can hold one captive.

clue.text: Husband having an uncommunicative disposition

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to husband is to save resources carefully
a ..., restrained manner

explanation.surface: A man described as having a quiet, withdrawn personality.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband supplies is to conserve them, and a guarded manner is called reticence or restraint.

clue.text: Leave the lady waiting, but counter criticism

definitions.meaning: to fail to turn up for a date
to defend oneself firmly

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their date waiting, yet defends themselves when criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to meet a date leaves them waiting in vain, and resisting criticism is holding firm against it.

clue.text: Poem in French takes note of both sexes

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem
en is the French word for in
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A poem written in French acknowledges men and women alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Having characteristics of male and female alike is the meaning of the adjective, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: New settler given allowance by the intelligence services

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: A newcomer gets funding from the secret services.
explanation.walkthrough: MI, Military Intelligence, is the British intelligence service, as in MI5 and MI6.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves to a new country to live is a migrant, a synonym for a new settler.

clue.text: Samuel raised a pet dog

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or a petty quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: A boy named Samuel brought up a pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' here is a fit of pique, as in 'in a pet', which is a TIFF; 'raised' turns SAM to MAS in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large powerful guard breed is an example of a dog.

clue.text: A situation found by the Italian missionary

parts.note: a post is a job or situation
le is the feminine plural word for the in Italian

explanation.surface: A missionary takes up a job alongside an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the early followers sent out to spread the gospel was a missionary.

clue.text: Minute cut-back in the paper

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is written backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a minuscule reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like 'tiny' but gives M; 'back' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: A written test taken at school is called a paper, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Gives the waiter little Japanese money when tight

parts.note: you tip a waiter, giving a small extra payment
Y is the abbreviation for yen, Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A diner tips generously in yen after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly drunk is being tight, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Only a fool takes cannabis

definitions.meaning: a stupid person, a dimwit
slang term for the drug

explanation.surface: Only an idiot would smoke marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is called a dope, and the same slang word names illegal drugs, especially cannabis.

clue.text: Failing to become a deputy

definitions.meaning: a weakness or moral fault
second in command

explanation.surface: A second-in-command is seen as a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral weakness is a vice, and the same word means a deputy, as in vice-captain.

clue.text: Examination taken by Violet and Virginia

parts.note: Vi is the short form of the name Violet
VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Two girls, Violet and Virginia, sit a test.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is an oral examination, especially in British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral test at university, the viva voce, is a kind of examination.

clue.text: Cryptic message about a German analgesic

indicators.note: about means going around, so the message encloses the German word

parts.note: a code is a secret message
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A coded message refers to a German painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling drug derived from opium is an analgesic.

clue.text: Amin to be put back in charge. That's silly

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: put back means the short word is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Restoring the Ugandan dictator to power would be foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foolish is silly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: As easy as pie to make a bite for tea

definitions.meaning: very simple to do
literally a portion of a sponge or fruit loaf eaten at teatime

explanation.surface: Making a teatime snack is described as extremely simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely simple is a doddle, idiom; literally a slice of a sweet baked treat.
